governanceNotes: D1 batch 62 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - muscle-hernias to peripheral-neuropathy (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the eleven-case literature review of muscle-herniation nerve entrapments (PMID 31325324), the operative popliteal common-peroneal case (PMID 7604332), and the MRI-confirmed superficial peroneal compression case (PMID 32190181).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) evidence class - one case plus an eleven-case review and single case reports spanning 1979-2019 with heterogeneous confirmation and publication bias toward unusual entrapments; (ii) anatomical scope - entrapments are fibular-nerve-specific and the general peripheral-neuropathy identity carries the proposition with that scope recorded; (iii) direction discipline - compartment syndrome is upstream of fascial defect in the located literature, so no compartment-syndrome edge was authored; (iv) constitutive boundary - the hernia's own mechanical pain is not authored as unexplained chronic pain; (v) diagnostic-mimic context - ankle-sprain and sciatica mimics are recorded so individual claims route through dynamic imaging.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Muscle herniation documents peripheral nerve entrapment at case-series and clinical-review level: the Muscle Nerve case with literature review identified eleven cases of nerve entrapment secondary to muscle herniation (unrelated to compartment syndrome) with the superficial fibular nerve the most commonly entrapped, patients presenting with pain, numbness, or paresthesias and a tender palpable mass with Tinel sign, responding well to fasciotomy (PMID 31325324), the popliteal case report documents gastrocnemius muscle herniation through a torn fascia compressing the common peroneal nerve with pseudoradicular symptoms relieved by fascial repair (PMID 7604332), and the radiology case report documents MRI-confirmed superficial peroneal nerve compression by peroneus brevis herniation (PMID 32190181); the relationship is recorded as documented mechanical-entrapment association at case level only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the located evidence is one case plus an eleven-case literature review and single case reports spanning decades with heterogeneous electrodiagnostic confirmation, so any individual neuropathy claim requires electrodiagnostic and imaging confirmation with radiculopathy, diabetic, and entrapment-at-other-sites exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A focal fascial defect allows muscle to bulge dynamically through the defect so the adjacent nerve (most commonly the superficial fibular nerve at the fibularis compartment) is compressed against fascia or bone and entrapment neuropathy with pain, numbness, and paresthesias results, the mechanical-entrapment route directly documented by the eleven-case review and the operative cases with symptom relief after fasciotomy or fascial repair, but whether this route produced any individual neuropathy remains hypothesized until electrodiagnostic and imaging records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at case-plus-small-review class only: the anchor review aggregates eleven cases published over decades with heterogeneous workup, the reported entrapments are anatomically specific (superficial fibular and common peroneal nerves) rather than general peripheral neuropathy, and no located cohort quantifies neuropathy incidence among muscle-hernia patients.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No cohort quantifies nerve-entrapment incidence among muscle-hernia patients; publication bias favors unusual entrapment cases; dynamic ultrasound and MRI confirmation varies across the case literature; compartment syndrome is the dominant fascial-defect context and was explicitly excluded from the anchor review; and lumbar radiculopathy, diabetic neuropathy, and fibular-head entrapment from other causes compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: lumbar radiculopathy mimicking peroneal symptoms (the anchor case's pseudoradicular framing)
common fibular nerve entrapment at the fibular head from other causes
chronic exertional compartment syndrome (the dominant fascial-defect context; direction runs compartment pressure to fascial defect, recorded as reverse framing)
tarsal tunnel and other distal entrapments

evidenceGaps: No cohort quantifies nerve-entrapment incidence among muscle-hernia patients; publication bias favors unusual entrapment cases; dynamic ultrasound and MRI confirmation varies across the case literature; compartment syndrome is the dominant fascial-defect context and was explicitly excluded from the anchor review; and lumbar radiculopathy, diabetic neuropathy, and fibular-head entrapment from other causes compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-plus-small-review class with the anatomical-scope limit carried openly: the eleven-case literature review identifies superficial fibular nerve entrapment as the most common muscle-hernia nerve lesion with fasciotomy response (PMID 31325324), the popliteal case documents common peroneal compression with symptom relief after fascial repair (PMID 7604332), and the MRI case documents peroneus brevis herniation compressing the superficial peroneal nerve (PMID 32190181); because the evidence is case class with publication bias toward unusual entrapments and the edge targets the general peripheral-neuropathy identity (no peroneal-specific identity exists in the catalog), the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through electrodiagnostic and imaging confirmation with radiculopathic, metabolic, and compartment-syndrome exclusion.

sourceReferences.citation: Tong O, Bieri P, Herskovitz S. Nerve entrapments related to muscle herniation Muscle Nerve. 2019 Oct;60(4):428-433. doi: 10.1002/mus.26643. PMID 31325324.
sourceReferences.note: Case report with literature review (Muscle Nerve, 2019): superficial fibular neuropathy from fibularis brevis herniation plus eleven identified cases of nerve entrapment secondary to muscle herniation unrelated to compartment syndrome; superficial fibular nerve most commonly entrapped; pain, numbness, paresthesias, Tinel sign; fasciotomy salutary; supports the bounded entrapment association only.
